The quick rundown and story of EXALT:

In the beginning, Sealand developed a new strain of cannabis. Sealand of course had no place to grow their product as it was just a platform in the middle of the ocean at the time. Liberland was a startup nation with a bit of land and very few people living on it. So Liberland made a deal to lease a portion of their land in a joint business venture with Sealand. For this, Liberland got a 35% share of the profits and rights to run experiments on the Sealand product, Sealand got 65%, and we were in business.

Later, Liberland lead scientist, Tim, unveiled a superior product (the new Sexual Tyrannosaurus weed strain which is still in use by EXALT to this day). Liberland increased the amount of land they leased, replaced the Seaweed (Sealand weed) with the Sexual Tyrannosaurus strain and negotiated a new 50/50 deal with Sealand. But Sealand generously offered 60/40 in Liberlands favor and Liberland accepted. So Liberland for a time operated 60% of the weed business.

A little later Liberland had an influx of people moving in. 9,000 libertarians moved in to claim their new homeland.

Okay, at this point Liberland had a problem. Liberland is actually prohibited by their constitution from operating any for-profit business as a state. Nobody cared or was even there to raise objection that the state was leasing their land and raising funds when there were only 5 legal citizens living in the country (the rest were employees). But with new people moving in and holding their government to strict constitutional standards, the 200-acre weed farm became a clear conflict.

EXALT Inc came into existence through pure entrepreneurial force of will. It was the perfect deal. The heavens aligned just right and I (as a player) decided to start a completely separate roleplay as a private company. It was a [win-win-win situation for everyone involved](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WPYz-bvypmU), the kind of opportunity that I thought some entrepreneur, somewhere out there, would take advantage of. Sealand got 45% share of the new company and a contract not to work against Sealand interests. Liberland secured a pledge to donate 45% of profits from the new company under their voluntary tax program and a contractual agreement not to work against Liberland interests. And these new guys just got 10% of the profits for basically nothing. Literally they talked their way into 10% profits of a highly profitable company that they previously had nothing to do with. Sealand of course welcomed a larger piece of a larger pie, Liberland got out of their constitutional conflict, and EXALT as a private company was able to start grow operations in multiple other legal countries (something I presume a state would not be welcome to do).

But these guys are NOT libertarians and do not represent Liberland. They are businessmen. At times I have even made them do things that no libertarian would do. For example they are getting into private military contracts - something abhorrent to libertarians. They hold no scruples or hesitation about working with governments for profit - also something abhorrent to libertarians. Liberland doesn't even recognize their Monsanto-style patents on the weed strain, as this is a subject of great controversy among libertarians (of course Liberland would never work against a company that is donating 45% of profits in tax revenue, but this also serves as some leverage for Liberland not to get stabbed in the back).

Seriously you guys, these EXALT guys are just in it for the money. They have always demonstrated loyalty to their friends but they are morally gray. This is a private company operating for private interests. So when I make a post saying EXALT does this or that, Liberland does not necessarily support these actions. Liberland as a state has shown themselves to be ideologically rigid libertarians, and often cannot condone what a private company does. Likewise EXALT probably thinks Liberland's ideological rigidity is silly and doesn't see the point.

Nope : it's time to use a less boneheaded nuclear reactor design.

No: solar won't allow for space travel. And we need a more consistent and controllable power generation method for base load than wind or solar. Batteries, like solar, are costly and have a toxic production path. Pumped hydro is a good energy storage solution for areas that have the geography, but most don't.

Energy use will almost certainly never decrease so we need, more than anything, cheap methods of power storage/production. Especially if we want to get away from cheap fossil fuels for energy and manufacturing.

Decentralizing power production is also a worthy goal that nuclear doesn't fulfil but I think the other pros for nuclear outweigh that con.

To me, phasing out nuclear because of problems with the existing style of reactor is shortsighted and, ultimately, throwing the baby out with the bathwater. Nuclear as an industry has the potential to cheaply, safely, efficiently, and cleanly generate all the power we could forseeably need.
